scriptVerdict: Migration script itself is clean: 7/7 stated purposes achieved, 6/6 pre + 7/7 post conditions pass, zero unintended on-chain writes. Exact full-balance USDC drain (128.572549) OLD->new, batchDonationSize restored 0->10, SYA nudge + pooler batchMinter repointed to new minter, old minter retired (nudge zeroed). All candidate findings are knock-on cluster/config issues, not defects in the migration logic.

candidates.title: Migration silently bricks the mint-sell-donate funder: its hardcoded BATCH_MINTER constant still points at the retired old minter
candidates.description: mint-sell-donate is the ongoing operational funder that tops up the BatchNFTMinter USDC pot (mint phUSD -> sUSDS -> USDS -> USDC via PSM buyGem). Its donation target `address constant BATCH_MINTER = 0x6e98...5071` (the OLD minter) is a compile-time constant with NO env override. It self-checks `require(IPoolerCfg(LIVE_POOLER).batchMinter() == BATCH_MINTER, "batchMinter != live pooler")` at line 308. This migration repoints `POOLER.batchMinter()` to the NEW minter. Consequently, the very next mint-sell-donate run reverts at line 308 before any funds move.
candidates.impact: Fail-SAFE, not fail-dangerous: the require aborts the run, so USDC is NEVER donated into the dead old contract (no stranded funds). BUT the protocol's only documented pot-refill path is rendered inoperable until someone edits the source constant, recompiles, and re-runs. The new minter's nudge pot stops being topped up beyond the one-time 128.57 USDC seed + per-mint donate-forward, degrading the nudge incentive over time. The migration ships no accompanying patch to this sibling and the closure has no automated linkage between them.
candidates.evidence: side-effects.json clusterChecks[0]; grep confirms BATCH_MINTER is `constant` at line 279 (not vm.envOr); preview trace shows POOLER.setBatchMinter(new) + post-flight pooler.batchMinter == new minter; mint-sell-donate line 308 asserts equality against the stale OLD constant.
candidates.recommendation: Either (a) make mint-sell-donate's BATCH_MINTER env/config-driven (read from live pooler.batchMinter() and assert it has code) so it tracks migrations automatically, or (b) include a source-bump of MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol (BATCH_MINTER -> new minter) as an explicit post-migration checklist/cluster step. Document the ordering dependency in the Story 057 plan.

candidates.title: MigrateBatchNFTMinter lacks a chainid guard, unlike its sibling funder
candidates.description: run() has no `require(block.chainid == 1)`; it relies solely on --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET and hardcoded mainnet address constants. The sibling MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter pins chainid (line 289), so this is an inconsistency in the same cluster. A misconfigured RPC env or a fat-fingered --fork-url would let the broadcast path execute against the wrong chain.
candidates.impact: Low: a broadcast against a non-mainnet chain would mostly revert on the first external call to a non-existent contract, and the broadcast requires a Ledger signature. But it removes a cheap, standard fail-fast guard the rest of the cluster relies on, and the repo CLAUDE.md Configuration-Safety section mandates an explicit network guard for real-network scripts.
candidates.evidence: intent.md access section; script lines 114-140 contain no chainid check; sibling MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol:289 `require(block.chainid == 1, ...)`.
candidates.recommendation: Add `require(block.chainid == 1, "expected mainnet (1)")` at the top of run() (or gate behind PREVIEW for local), matching the sibling and the repo's Configuration-Safety gate.

candidates.title: New BatchNFTMinter is deployed unpausable (pauser left at address(0))
candidates.description: The migration deliberately does NOT call setPauser, leaving the new minter's `pauser == address(0)` to 'match the current live instance' (verified on fork: old minter pauser == 0x0). The new minter holds the full nudge pot and its batchMint nudge payout is gated only on a numeric `count >= nudgeSize` threshold. With pauser == 0, pause()/unpause() are permanently unusable, so there is no circuit breaker.
candidates.impact: Low and largely pre-existing (the old instance was equally unpausable, so this migration does not regress security posture). Flagged as an intent/centralization-safety observation: 'match current' silently re-adopts a no-circuit-breaker config for a fund-holding contract.
candidates.evidence: BatchNFTMinter.sol:150-153 (setPauser) and modifier onlyPauser at 112-115; migration _deployAndConfigure (lines 154-168) omits setPauser by design; cast confirms OLD minter pauser == 0x0.
candidates.recommendation: Confirm with the operator whether the global Phoenix Pauser should be wired into the new minter. If unpausable-by-design is intentional, document the accepted risk explicitly; otherwise add setPauser(globalPauser) to the migration.
